_comment: Battle AI phase 4 (docs/battle-ai-design.md): player delegation. A custom 2-vs-1 scenario (not the default 5v5 line) so the delegated pair and the single enemy read clearly at this zoom. Team 0 spawns at the SMALLER y (Battle._spawn_scenario always faces team 0 Vector2.DOWN, toward +y) with the enemy at a LARGER y below it, matching the game's standard team0-above/team1-below layout, so both units march straight toward the enemy with no facing reversal. The two team-0 units are 300 wu apart (x=450/750) -- an Infantry formation's own bbox is ~120 wu wide, so anything much narrower than that leaves the two blocks physically overlapping at spawn; CI's demo-defect scan caught exactly that on an earlier staging that placed them only 100 wu apart (x=500/600), which showed up as each unit's OWN soldier-body overlap metric failing (cross-unit friendly-crowding pressure at the touching edge compresses each unit's own adjacent ranks, not a Subcommander/delegation bug -- confirmed by an isolated single-unit control scenario, which shows zero drift with no neighbor nearby). Box-selects both team-0 units, delegates them to AI subcommander group 5 (Ctrl+Shift+5) so they advance and engage the enemy on their own -- no further orders from the player -- then, with the same selection still active, issues an immediate Hold stance (Ctrl+H) to take manual control back, per the design doc's 'a manual player order to a delegated unit always overrides the subcommander's directive'. Driven live through the real SelectionManager by tools/demo/DemoInputRecorder.gd; world coordinates; physics ticks (60/s).
